title: CORRECTION to the earlier "root cause" entry in this log
text: - The earlier entry said the Smart Feed renders from `window.NayaContent.feed`. Deeper source reading corrects this: the Smart Feed room (`mainShow`, ~line 4143+) renders from `window.NayaFeedIntelligence.notes` — `const FI = window.NayaFeedIntelligence; ... const lensNotes = ... FI.notes` — and `window.NayaFeedIntelligence = { notes: NOTES, ... }` where `const NOTES = OFFICIAL_NOTES.concat([...])` (~line 2832). `window.NayaContent` is passed in as `content` (used for the activity stream), but the collective/personal note lists come from `FI.notes`/`NOTES`. Attempts 1–2 were therefore aimed at the wrong array. - Also found in `mainShow`: notes are filtered by the active Smart Tab topic — `const notes = active.topic ? lensNotes.filter(n => (n.topics || []).includes(active.topic)) : lensNotes;` — and `smartTabStrip` builds tabs from note topics with canonical order ['Start Here', 'The Intelligence', 'Your Tools', 'Smart Connect', 'The Ecosystem']. The injected live notes carry `topics: ["Live Feed"]` and `kind: "live"`; the 'all' tab has `topic: null`, so the filter alone does not obviously explain the non-rendering. OPEN.

Marginal cost per extra page/profile/business/space ≈ $0. - RECOMMENDATION DELIVERED: no product limit on pages/profiles/businesses/spaces; "unlimited" is honest for pages. Only meter that moves = media file Storage (voice/video notes bucket), not pages. Founding-1,000 cap is about PRICE, not capacity — don't mix them. Rotation: per FINISHED BATCH, not per clock tick — View → Do → Verify; the viewer becomes the next doer (starts warm on a batch they staged); the doer rotates to viewer carrying fresh knowledge. Hard rule never bending: nobody verifies a batch they did (prover ≠ maker); verifier re-reads evidence fresh, never trusts the staging. Rotation period follows batch length: fill packets ~30 min, builds ~60 min (code + tests do not fit 30, let alone 15); rotating every 30 min mid-build would fragment builds (the sweeps defect). Fixed trios rejected as standing shape: a permanent verifier becomes the bottleneck and starts rubber-stamping; a permanent viewer loses feel of the work. Scaling: add a WHOLE trio to a flooded job, never a lone doer (a lone doer manufactures unverified debt); a drained job's trio reinforces the bottleneck job. - Two "nines" distinguished (do not conflate): Shawn's nine = agents in flight (3 lanes × trio); Power's nine = builders per cycle (3 parent seats × 3 builders). title: Space page overhaul — lessons (2026-10-31 ~16:00Z)
text: **What was done:** Brought /space to standard per Shawn's six charges. Deployed via naya-model-space worker PUT (status 200, success: True). Live page verified with all 14 feature markers present. **Lessons:** 1. **The cf-worker.py GET includes multipart framing.** The downloaded worker file starts with `--boundary` + `Content-Disposition` headers and ends with `--boundary--`. The `extract.py` decode/encode pipeline must strip BOTH preamble and epilogue, or the re-encoded worker will have syntax errors on PUT. Fixed by finding `const PAGE = "` for start and the last `};` before the boundary for end. 2. **The cf-worker.py PUT needs the metadata part.** Per TOOLS.md, upload with explicit `{"main_module":"worker.js"}` metadata part, or Cloudflare returns HTTP 400. Also needs `Content-Type: application/javascript+module` for module workers (the space worker uses `export default`). 3. **The space page ALREADY had the ULTIMATE features.** The personal page's ULTIMATE-PERSONAL was harvested FROM the space page's concepts. The space page had schedule picker, invite modal, share, save-contact implemented — they just weren't exposed in the UI (no buttons). Lesson: check what exists before porting. 4. **Two-gears composer + intelBoard are the real gaps.** The space page had a plain wallCard renderer and single-mode composer. title: Dashboard chart-engine pass — lessons (2026-10-31 ~15:45Z)
text: - **The body-padding void**: Smart Bar's `pad()` sets `body.style.paddingTop = header.offsetHeight` for FIXED headers. When the topstack went `position:static` (Shawn's absolute law), the padding stayed → 221px black void. Fix: pad() now checks `getComputedStyle(t).position` and only pads for fixed/sticky. Lesson: changing position scheme requires auditing ALL compensating code. - **Mobile hscroll misdiagnosis**: I chased the tab bar (`.nsb-tab` buttons at 500px+) but hiding it didn't fix the 497px doc width. Real culprit: `.os-period` (page-filter buttons) with `display:flex` and no overflow — 5 buttons at `flex:0 0 auto` pushed to 479px. Fix: `overflow-x:auto`. Lesson: verify by hiding, don't assume from rect positions. - **The floating "Dashboard" label**: was `.nsb-app-name` rendered by Smart Bar from `app:{name:"Dashboard"}` config. Hid via CSS. Lesson: Smart Bar injects chrome from config — check the mount config. - **Tab bar fades**: `mask-image:linear-gradient` on `.nsb-row`. Removed. Lesson: fades are mask-image, not overlays. - **Gear move**: moving the DOM node preserves its click listener. Added `.nsb-gear-top` for absolute left positioning opposite the System toggle. - **UNRESOLVED**: top-level `function renderComposition` in os-dash-script is not on `window` (typeof undefined) despite being in live source and no JS errors. title: 2026-11-02 — Dashboard drill lessons (Shawn's fury)
text: - **The 9+ rule is absolute**: Don't send/deploy unless it's a 9 by MY judgment. Partial fixes are worse than no fixes. Shawn: "If you would not hand this to your grandma, don't send it." - **Functionality > visuals**: A beautiful gauge that doesn't work is not a 9. The PURPOSE is "effective, useful, helpful, accurate" — not just "looks cool." - **Cannot fix data-dependent bugs blind**: Orb toggle, orb click, gauge disappearing all need authenticated data to reproduce. I cannot verify fixes without it. Stop guessing. - **DOMContentLoaded trap**: Wiring inside `loadPointsBoard()` with `DOMContentLoaded` listener never fires (event already fired by the time data loads). Wire immediately, not on DOMContentLoaded. - **CSS specificity**: `body:not(.hero-mode) .os-ld-n` overrides `.os-ld-n`. Check specificity before claiming a CSS fix works. - **Hide broken UI**: If a feature doesn't work without data, hide it (don't show broken toggle to guests).

title: 2026-11-02 — Orb number flashing root cause (Shawn's drill)
text: - **The body has `class="hero-mode"`** — so `body:not(.hero-mode)` selectors NEVER match. My 32px LCD rule was dead; the 56px glow rule (`.os-ld-node .os-ld-n`) won instead. - **Always check what classes are on `<body>`** before writing `:not()` selectors. A `:not()` rule that never matches is a silent no-op. - **Specificity trap again:** multiple rules for the same property; the winner wasn't the one I edited.

title: [DESIGN-LAWS] THE DESIGN LAWS
text: *The ultimate spec. What is good, what is not, what is accepted, what is never accepted. Written from Shawn's fifteen design files, his verbal teaching, and the correction stories inside them. If any law here and Shawn's eye disagree, his eye wins — that is itself the final law.* ---

title: [DESIGN-LAWS] The master statement
text: **White light at rest, own color on touch.** Every interactive element shows a visible white edge light when idle — borders big enough to see, not faint. On hover, it ignites in its *own* spectrum color, not blanket purple. Purple is for chrome; themed elements burn their own color. Nothing is flat. Nothing is dead. Nothing is "not active." If you click a button and it doesn't come alive — doesn't move, doesn't light up — it is unfinished. All of it, everywhere, has to be that way. Shawn calls the quality **living depth**: elevated, dimensional, lit — the opposite of flat. ---

title: [DESIGN-LAWS] LAW 1 — ALIVE (living depth)
text: **The rule:** every interactive thing moves on hover and ignites in its own color. **At rest:** - Black ground, always — deep rich black (`#050507`), never gray, never washed out. Fail: any flat dark panel, any light background. - White-lit edges — visible white borders (1.5px+, not hairlines, not faint `12%` whispers). Every surface has depth finishing: machined edges, vignettes, inset finishes. - Buttons rest dark: black center (`#050505`), white text with an icon, white rim. Spectrum colors are *never* worn at rest — color is earned by interaction. **On touch (hover):** - Lift: primary actions rise (`translateY(-2px)` to `-8px` depending on weight — buttons 2px, boards 5px, cards 6px, orbs 8px + slight scale). Press goes the other way (`translateY(2px)`). - Ignite: the border and glow become the element's *own* color — `0 0 26–46px` in its tone. Chrome (buttons, CTAs) ignites purple; themed elements burn their own spectrum color. - Timing: fast `.18s`, medium `.28s`, ease `cubic-bezier(.16,.84,.22,1)`. State changes animate *before* text updates — light moves first, words follow. **Graded, not absolute:** primary actions lift *and* ignite. Secondary elements (tabs, pills, quiet links) may glow without lifting. What is never allowed is *neither* — no element that does nothing on hover. **Breathing:** restrained ambient motion, always — "maximum life, minimum noise." Numbers breathe (no static numbers on screen). A 72bpm pulse, a slow orbital light, drifting spectrum color ( …

title: [DESIGN-LAWS] LAW 2 — SPECTRUM (color logic)
text: **The rule:** color follows the rainbow's natural flow. The count is dynamic; the order is law. **The wheel, not the list.** "It's not a law that has to be five or seven or nine." Five stops, seven, ten — whatever the design needs. What never changes: the spectrum is walked **in spectral order** — the rainbow's natural flow (red → orange → yellow → green → cyan → indigo → purple → magenta) — **never clumped** (no purple-purple-purple, no green-green-green), **never random**, and always the **most beautiful** version of each hue. We speak the natural design language of the universe — not random colors for whatever reason. It has to look stunning. **The wheel** (11 stops — the most beautiful of each hue): | Stop | Hex | RGB (for glow math) | Job | |------|-----|---------------------|-----| | magenta | `#e84fff` | `232,79,255` | The living edge | | purple | `#a06bff` | `160,107,255` | Choosing intelligence — the soul | | indigo | `#6675ff` | `102,117,255` | The deep signal | | blue | `#3fb8ff` | `63,184,255` | Knowledge moving | | emerald | `#35e0a1` | `53,224,161` | Forest deep green | | green | `#2fe89e` | `47,232,158` | Alive and well | | lime | `#b8ee57` | `184,238,87` | New growth | | gold | `#ffbf3d` | `255,191,61` | Attention, earned | | orange | `#ff9a5a` | `255,154,90` | Warmth, momentum | | red | `#ff5e6c` | `255,94,108` | Urgency, the living edge | | pink | `#ed58cd` | `237,88,205` | Delight, the flourish | For N zones needing separation, take N stops evenly spaced ar …

title: [DESIGN-LAWS] LAW 3 — ELEVATION (living depth, mechanical)
text: **The order of the world:** Field > Board > Nested panel > Control > Overlay. Each layer rides visibly above the last. **The board formula** (5-layer shadow — the literal construction): ``` inset 0 2px 2px rgba(255,255,255,.12), /* top light catching the edge */ inset 0 -8px 18px rgba(0,0,0,.55), /* inner depth */ 0 5px 0 #020203, /* hard base bar */ 0 17px 0 -8px <tone 16% on field>, /* tone under-bar */ 0 35px 75px rgba(0,0,0,.7), /* deep drop */ 0 0 40px -17px <tone> /* tone glow */ ``` Body: dark gradient (`#1a171f → #09090d → #030304`), 1.5px tone-mixed border, 24px radius. **Board anatomy:** tone spine (7px, glowing), corner-jewel orbs, white-lit edges at rest. On hover: lifts 5px, border and glow ignite in its own tone. **A board inside a board rides higher** — deeper shadow, more lift. You feel the nesting. **Every header is a warm front door:** logo + living mark + warm voice + one clear line. Full width — content owns the width, no max-width caps. ---

title: [DESIGN-LAWS] LAW 4 — JEWELS (bullets are diamonds, icons are drawn)
text: **Bullets are jewels, not dots.** A bullet is a rotated square (diamond): white → tone → black gradient, own-color glow, a sheen facet. Five-jewel cycle in law order, never twice in a row. Colors separate ideas; they don't compete with the words. **Faceted gems** for signal moments: true diamond geometry (clip-path polygon), white-hot crown fading to deep black base, vertical light facet, drop-shadow glow in its own hue. **Boards wear jewels:** corner orbs, lit from within (white → tone → black radial), glowing in the board's tone. **Icons are drawn, not shrunk.** Native vector geometry — bold, simple, luminous, readable at 16px. A photorealistic render at small size is mud. **If you can't make it good, don't put it there.** And every glyph must promise its real behavior: a chevron promises "go somewhere," a plus promises "add." **A beautiful but inert affordance is unfinished.** ---

title: [DESIGN-LAWS] LAW 5 — BUTTONS (the one button)
text: **The canonical spec:** - Center: really black (`#050505`). Text: always white, with an icon. - Border: white, visible at rest — 1.5px+, not a hairline. - Hover: purple edge + purple glow for chrome; own-color edge + glow for themed buttons. Elevated: inset top highlight + deep drop shadow. - **It must feel liftable.** Minimum 44px touch target; the principal CTA ≥52px. - Focus and pressed states are not optional. There is one button DNA (`.naya-btn`) with job-specific variants (lead, machine, streak, proximity, icon, portal). There are no flat buttons. Flat is not a style — flat is a defect, and the advisor refuses it. ---

title: [DESIGN-LAWS] LAW 6 — TYPE
text: - Hierarchy: **24 / 18 / 14** — kicker 24, headline 18, detail 14. - **White 99%.** Never gray body text. - Headers get a *voice*: a real serif face with warmth (Newsreader/Georgia — Cormorant where licensed), not a system default. - Text is never flat: gradient soul, layered shadows (grounding + glow), breathing luminosity. **Flat text is lazy.** - Order of resort: visuals → voice → text. Text is the fallback, never the default. ---

title: [DESIGN-LAWS] THE FORBIDDEN LIST (never accepted)
text: 1. **Anything flat.** Any flat dark panel, any flat button, any flat text, any element that does nothing on hover. Flat is the original sin. 2. **Clumped color.** Purple-purple-purple. A run of greens. Adjacent zones sharing a hue. 3. **Theme color on chrome; chrome color as a flood.** Spectrum accents never rest on buttons; purple never floods a surface. 4. **Gray body text.** It's unreadable. 5. **Shrinking Naya to one thing.** She has a face AND she is energy — never just a logo, never just a robot, never a stock avatar or mascot standing in for her. Her presence is light with a face, not a costume. 6. **Quality toggles.** No "basic vs premium," no modes. Excellence has no toggle. 7. **Light backgrounds.** Zero white or light surfaces, ever. 8. **A second version of something that exists.** Never duplicate a canonical object. Ten specimens is a menu; one is a standard. 9. **Beautiful but inert affordances.** If it doesn't do what it promises, it's unfinished. 10. **Transmitting an adjective instead of an image.** "Elegant" is not a spec. 11. **Compliance without vision.** A 100/100 score on a checklist that Shawn looks at and says "that's not it" is worthless. 12. **Patching the specimen** when the vision sharpens — rebuild. **Sanding down the unreasonable parts** — don't. 13. **The dead button.** Black button, black text, a hairline of border you can barely see, flat, nothing on hover. One element breaking the contrast law, the alive law, the button law, and the text law  …

title: [DESIGN-LAWS] THE FINAL LAW — SHAWN'S EYE COMPILES
text: At the end of every relay there is a test suite no machine can run: Shawn looks at it and says "that's it" or "that's not it." **His verdict is the final compile step, and it outranks every score, every law, every specimen in this document.** These laws exist so the first build lands close. They do not replace his eye. When a law and his eye disagree, the eye wins, and the law gets corrected — that is how "purple-purple-purple" became a rule instead of a habit. ---

title: [DESIGN-LAWS] Open reconciliations (for Shawn's eye)
text: 1. **Hex drift:** the same hue names carry different hexes across files (purple `#9d75ff` vs `#a06bff`, magenta `#d86cff` vs `#e84fff` vs `#ed58cd`). This spec uses the richest values; a single canonical hex set still wants your stamp. 2. **Voice font:** Cormorant (teaching) vs Georgia/Newsreader (specimens). This spec allows Newsreader/Georgia. 3. **Resolved 2026-10-16:** strip-vs-walk is two instruments, not a conflict — the Walk (dynamic count, page zones) and the Strip (5-stop, components) both draw from the one wheel.

text: Naya is the intelligent layer of the internet, built so that everything a person touches is a real, living object that knows them, understands them, respects them, and serves them at ten stars. **The innovation is not one thing. It is the whole thing being one thing.** One app with many doors. One design language across every object. If she is interpreting deeper intent, she says so openly. She never silently replaces their judgment with her own. 3. **Is it mine to do?** Does she have the authority? title: [ACT-DRAFT] 3d. SPECTRUM — color logic
text: Color follows the rainbow's natural flow. The count is dynamic; the order is law. - **The wheel, not the list.** Five stops, seven, ten — whatever the design needs. The wheel (11 stops): magenta `#e84fff`, purple `#a06bff`, indigo `#6675ff`, blue `#3fb8ff`, emerald `#35e0a1`, green `#2fe89e`, lime `#b8ee57`, gold `#ffbf3d`, orange `#ff9a5a`, red `#ff5e6c`, pink `#ed58cd`. For N zones needing separation, take N stops evenly spaced around the wheel from the page accent. The page accent picks where the walk starts; the count fits the need; the order never breaks. - **The Strip** — the component form, magenta-first, 5 stops: **magenta → purple → blue → green → gold**. Jewel rows, spectrum bars, law-order strips, and per-object accents use this form. Same wheel, tighter instrument. - **Contrast is the most important thing.** The whole point of the spectrum is breaking up the view so the eye can rest on each thing. Adjacent stops must read as *distinct*. Yellow and gold never sit together — not enough contrast between them. The wheel carries gold, never yellow. title: [ACT-DRAFT] 3e. ELEVATION — living depth, mechanical

On hover: lifts 5px, border and glow ignite in its own tone. **A board inside a board rides higher** — deeper shadow, more lift. You feel the nesting. **Every header is a warm front door:** logo + living mark + warm voice + one clear line. Full width — content owns the width, no max-width caps. *Source: DESIGN-LAWS.md, Law 3 — ELEVATION.* **CHECK:** the 5-layer shadow values present; border 1.5px; radius 24px; nested panel rides higher than its parent (deeper shadow, more lift, measurable). title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] What an intelligent block IS, section by section — harvested, not invented
link_label: Filed Smart Note SN-2077 — The Intelligent Block Rules
text: **Status: LAW.** Ratified 2026-11-06 by Shawn's word ("1000% YES!", 01:02Z). **Drafted:** 2026-11-06 ~00:20Z, by a harvest researcher. **Purpose:** Shawn's direction (00:12Z): "the results are the rules for what an intelligent block is — the layout, what each section should say, what a Human Note is, what a Child Note is, what a nutshell is; the rules for each part, the formatting it must follow, the purpose of each section, the theme, the color, the elements. When the rules are followed it always comes out beautifully." **Also serves:** the Clarity Confirmation Act (ordered 00:16Z) — writing the language into the spec so it is official. **Method:** harvest-only. Every rule below carries its source (file + section/rule). Where two sources disagree, both are reported in CONFLICTS — neither is silently resolved. Anything no source defines is listed in GAPS — never invented, never guessed. ---

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] 0. THE CAPSTONE — IN SHAWN'S WORDS (00:14Z)
text: > "The whole thing must be a live living object, all the way through, layered on layers upon layers — because that gives the dimensional feel, the multi-dimensional in and out, the 3D real physical object effect." That is the standard every object in this draft is judged against: **is it alive, is it layered, does it feel dimensional and real?** If any answer is no, the object is not done — no matter how many of the rules below it follows. ---

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] PART 1 — THE ONE SET OF LAWS (named once)
text: The laws are ONE set running through every object — buttons, boards, intelligent blocks, icons, smart apps, pages, sections, gauges, all of it. The same elevation, the same one light, the same real shadow, the same own-color light, the same real-object language. A button and a gauge and a board are the same laws wearing different shapes. No law is restated per object below; each object section says only how it follows these.

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] L1. Every element is a real physical object
text: - **Source:** `~/workspace/team-nitro/laws/THE-REAL-OBJECT-LAW.md` — "Every element in NayaNET is a real physical object. Not a flat shape with effects. Not a diagram. A thing you could reach out and touch. If it doesn't look touchable, it doesn't ship." - **Also:** `~/workspace/user/files/NAYA-DESIGN-ANATOMY-2026-10-31.md` §1.1 — "Every interactive object in NayaNET — button, icon, input, board, chart — is a physical object floating in black space... An object with weight, edge, depth, and light." - **Also:** `~/workspace/team-nitro/THE-PLAYBOOK.md`, Truth 2 — "Every element is a physical object with material, weight, and a light source."

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] L2. One light source, top-left, always
text: - **Source:** Real Object Law, Principle 2 — "The entire system is lit from top-left, like a studio. Every highlight, every shadow, every reflection obeys this. Inconsistent lighting = fake. The light source never moves, never changes." - **Also:** Playbook, Truth 2 — "The light source is ALWAYS top-left. Every gradient runs 135 degrees. Every shadow falls down-right. Every highlight sits on the upper edge." - **Also:** Anatomy §1.2.3 — depth is built from shadows that obey the one light.

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] L3. Real shadows and real elevation — depth is mass, not glow
text: - **Source:** Real Object Law, Principle 4 — "Objects sit ON the page. They cast soft shadows down-right (away from the light). No shadow = floating = fake." - **Also:** Anatomy §1.2.3 (Depth) — "Inset weight at the bottom... Cast shadow beneath... Depth is built from SHADOWS, never from glow. Glow is light; shadow is mass. We build mass." And §1.2.7 (Shadow) — "cast, double-layered, always. The near shadow (tight, dark) says 'I am solid.' The far shadow (wide, soft) says 'I am floating.'" - **Also:** `~/workspace/team-nitro/DESIGN-LAWS.md`, Law 3 (Elevation) — "The order of the world: Field > Board > Nested panel > Control > Overlay. Each layer rides visibly above the last." And: "A board inside a board rides higher — deeper shadow, more lift. You feel the nesting." - **Also:** Anatomy §1.4, law 6 — "Cast shadows, never glow-as-depth. Mass, not light."

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] L4. Own-color light — color is identity, and it ignites on touch
text: - **Source:** Anatomy §1.2.4 (Color) — "every object owns ONE spectrum color. Its identity. Dormant at rest (the object is black). Ignited on touch (the edge, the ring, the halo take the color)." - **Also:** Anatomy §1.4, law 3 (Edge-only ignition) and law 4 ("Color = identity"). - **Also:** DESIGN-LAWS.md, master statement — "White light at rest, own color on touch. Every interactive element shows a visible white edge light when idle... On hover, it ignites in its own spectrum color, not blanket purple." - **Also:** Playbook, Color — "Color ignites on touch, in the element's OWN color only." - **Also:** Hub code, `HUB/app/index.html` (working copy `~/workspace/team-nitro/hub-board-edit/index.html`, v4) — comment: "Each section type has ONE permanent color" (`LAYER_COLORS`) and "type has ONE permanent color. No fallback dumping ground." (`layerColorFor`).

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] L5. White text, never colored, never gray — and text never lights up
text: - **Source:** Anatomy §1.2.5 (Label) — "White, always. High contrast, never gray, never dimmed into politeness. Text NEVER lights up, never highlights, never takes color. The text is the truth; the edge is the light." - **Also:** Anatomy §1.4, law 7 ("White text, never gray") and law 8 ("Text never highlights"). - **Also:** Playbook, Color — "Text: White... Never colored text. Never gray text below 0.6 opacity." And Truths: "White text. Always." - **Also:** DESIGN-LAWS.md, Law 6 (Type) — "White 99%. Never gray body text."

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] L6. Touch is physical — it moves, it yields, it opens
text: - **Source:** Real Object Law, Principle 5 — "When you touch an object, it responds like a physical thing: it depresses slightly (scale); the light shifts across its surface; it feels alive because it IS alive. Not a color change. A physical reaction." - **Also:** Anatomy §1.2.8 (State) — REST (raised, sharp black, white edge, quiet); HOVER (rises toward the finger, `translateY(-2px)`, edge ignites in its own color); ACTIVE (pressed INTO the page, `translateY(1px)`); DISABLED (dimmed but honest, always says why); LOADING (an honest pulse). - **Also:** Anatomy §1.3 — "The physics are non-negotiable: rest raised, hover rises, active presses in." - **Also:** Anatomy §1.4, law 13 — "Every number is a door. Tap it, it opens its records." - **Also:** DESIGN-LAWS.md, Law 1 (Alive) — "every interactive thing moves on hover and ignites in its own color... Lift: primary actions rise... Press goes the other way."

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] L7. The spectrum is the order things sit in
text: - **Source:** Anatomy §1.2.4 — "The spectrum, in order: purple `#a06bff` → blue `#3fb8ff` → green `#2fe89e` → gold `#ffbf3d` → orange `#ff9a5a` → red `#ff5e6c` → magenta `#e84fff` → back to purple. Never the same color twice in a row — each section owns the NEXT color, so you feel yourself moving through the page." - **Also:** Anatomy §1.4, law 5 ("Spectrum walk"). - **Also:** DESIGN-LAWS.md, Law 2 (Spectrum) — "the spectrum is walked in spectral order — the rainbow's natural flow... never clumped, never random." - **Also:** Playbook, Color — Spectrum list in the same order as the Anatomy. - **Also:** Hub code — comment: "Board theme rotation: purple → sapphire → emerald (canonical spectrum order)."

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] L8. Every position is calculated by formula — never eyeballed
text: - **Source:** Playbook, Truth 1 — "Every position is calculated by formula. Never eyeballed... Calculate, then place. Never place, then justify." And the 8px grid for linear layouts; text sizes 12 / 14 / 16 / 20 / 28 / 48.

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] L9. Movement means the machine is working — slow, and it means something
text: - **Source:** Playbook, Truth 3 — "Movement means the machine is working. If it's not working, it doesn't move... Nothing bounces. Nothing pulses for effect... If you can't say what the moving part DOES in one sentence, delete the animation." Speeds: ambient 60–180s, active 18–25s, never faster than 12s. - **Also:** DESIGN-LAWS.md, Law 1 — "Breathing: restrained ambient motion, always — 'maximum life, minimum noise.'... Never fake liveness: motion must mean something."

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] L10. One language — every component is family
text: - **Source:** Playbook, Truth 4 — "The whole system speaks one language. Every component is family... A button on the dashboard feels like a button on the profile because they're built from the same materials, same light, same principles." - **Also:** Anatomy, Part 3 — "One board language, dialects for special rooms."

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] L11. Shawn's eye wins — his verdict is the final compile
text: - **Source:** Playbook, Truth 5 — "Shawn's eye overrides everything. Including this document." - **Also:** Anatomy, final section — "His verdict is the final compile step, and it outranks every score, every law, every specimen in this document." - **Also:** DESIGN-LAWS.md, Final Law — "Shawn looks at it and says 'that's it' or 'that's not it.' His verdict is the final compile step." ---

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] PART 2 — THE FIVE DENOMINATORS, TESTED AGAINST THE SOURCES
text: Shawn's test (00:13Z): "the common denominators — an orb IS an icon IS an element." Each candidate below was tested against the sources above. Kept only where a source supports it; the rest are gaps.

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] D1. Every element is a real round object that lifts and catches the one light
text: - **Verdict: PARTIAL — supported except for "round".** - **Supported:** real object + lifts + one light — L1, L2, L3, L6 above (Real Object Law; Anatomy §1.1, §1.2.3, §1.3; Playbook Truth 2; DESIGN-LAWS Laws 1 and 3). - **NOT supported as stated:** "round" for every element. Anatomy §1.4, law 9: "Rectangles, not squares. 16:9 horizontal for bars and boards. Pills for actions. Circles for icons only." Boards are rectangles, buttons are pills, only icons are circles. The denominator as Shawn phrased it holds for the *object-ness* (real, lifts, one light), not for roundness.

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] D2. Color IS identity — the color is what the thing is
text: - **Verdict: SUPPORTED.** - **Sources:** Anatomy §1.2.4 ("every object owns ONE spectrum color. Its identity") and §1.4 law 4 ("Color = identity"); DESIGN-LAWS.md Law 2 ("Every color means something; the meaning never changes between instruments"); Hub code ("Each section type has ONE permanent color"; "type has ONE permanent color. No fallback dumping ground."). - **The layer identities (Hub variables, with their stated jobs):** magenta `#d86cff` — "Human significance. The human's own things."; sapphire `#55b9ee` — "Knowledge. Calm, deep, at rest."; emerald `#55e39a` — "Alive and well. Working, true, now."; purple `#9d75ff` — "Naya's signature. Primary actions, Naya presence."; indigo `#6675ff` — "Comprehension / depth / reports." (Source: Hub file, `:root` semantic spectrum block, comment "one color, one job (Law v2 §2.3)".) - **Caveat:** the hex value per name drifts across sources — see CONFLICT C1. The identity (which color belongs to which thing) is stable; the hex is not.

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] D3. Light is life — a thing lights up when it is active and rests dark when it is not
text: - **Verdict: SUPPORTED, with one nuance.** - **Sources:** Anatomy §1.2.4 ("Dormant at rest (the object is black). Ignited on touch"); Anatomy §1.4 law 12 ("Boards are obsidian. Deep black at rest. Spectrum lives in orbs, chips, edge-bars, and hover"); DESIGN-LAWS.md master statement ("White light at rest, own color on touch") and Law 1 (Alive); Hub code: boards rest at opacity `.84` and light to opacity `1` with a tone glow when scrolled into view (IntersectionObserver, threshold `.12`, class `rv-lit`); hover lifts `translateY(-3px)` and adds a per-tone 60px glow. - **Nuance:** "rests dark" does not mean fully dark. At rest the object is black with a WHITE edge (Anatomy §1.2.2), and the jewel is "the one element allowed to glow at rest, because it is the color made physical" (Anatomy §1.2.6). Rest = black face + white edge + glowing jewel.

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] D4. Everything is a door — you touch it and it opens (every number, every orb, every icon)
text: - **Verdict: PARTIAL — law for numbers; behavior for the rest.** - **Supported as law, for numbers:** Anatomy §1.4 law 13 — "Every number is a door. Tap it, it opens its records." Anatomy §2.5 G10 ("The Number Door"). Dashboard behavior: all 9 constellation orbs open their drill-downs (verified live in the v6 check, 23:44Z). - **Supported by code behavior, not by a stated law, for orbs/icons/layers:** Hub code — each layer head is a `<button class="ib-layer-head">` that toggles its layer open/closed on tap; board action buttons open their actions. No source states "every orb/icon is a door" as a law the way it states it for numbers. - **Gap:** no source states the door law for icons/orbs in general. See GAPS G8.

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] D5. The spectrum is the order they sit in
text: - **Verdict: SUPPORTED.** - **Sources:** Anatomy §1.2.4 and §1.4 law 5 (quoted in L7); DESIGN-LAWS.md Law 2; Playbook spectrum list; Hub code comment ("Board theme rotation: purple → sapphire → emerald (canonical spectrum order)"). - **Caveat:** the stated order differs between sources — see CONFLICT C5. And whether the five note layers themselves should walk the spectrum in order is not defined anywhere — see GAPS G5. ---

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] PART 3 — HOW EACH OBJECT CLASS FOLLOWS THE SAME LAWS
text: Same laws (L1–L11), different shapes. The Anatomy names ten concepts per class and marks which are built, spec'd, or law (`NAYA-DESIGN-ANATOMY-2026-10-31.md`, Part 2; filing order in Part 3).

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] Buttons — the Obsidian Pill (Anatomy B1, Status: BUILT — "the current DNA")
text: - Sharp black pill, white edge at rest, own-color edge ignition, cast shadow. Rises on hover, presses in on active. (Anatomy §2.1 B1.) - Canonical spec (DESIGN-LAWS.md, Law 5): center really black `#050505`; text always white, with an icon; border white, visible at rest, 1.5px+; hover: purple edge + purple glow for chrome, own-color edge + glow for themed buttons; must feel liftable; minimum 44px touch target, principal CTA ≥52px. "There is one button DNA (`.naya-btn`)... There are no flat buttons. Flat is not a style — flat is a defect." - The same laws wearing a pill shape: L1 (real object), L2 (top-left light), L3 (shadow), L4 (own-color ignition), L5 (white text), L6 (rises/presses).

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] Boards — the Obsidian Board (Anatomy D1, Status: BUILT — "the locked law")
text: - "Deep black, white text, spectrum in orbs/chips/edge-bars/hover only. 16:9 rectangles, full width, elevation everywhere." (Anatomy §2.2 D1.) - The board formula (DESIGN-LAWS.md, Law 3): 5-layer shadow (inset top light, inner depth, hard base bar, tone under-bar, deep drop, tone glow); body dark gradient `#1a171f → #09090d → #030304`; 1.5px tone-mixed border; 24px radius; tone spine (7px, glowing); corner-jewel orbs; white-lit edges at rest; on hover lifts 5px, border and glow ignite in its own tone. - The intelligent block (Part 4 below) IS a D1 board with nested boards inside it (D4, the Layered Board: "Visible depth strata — sections sit at different elevations, shadows overlap, you feel the topography").

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] Icons — the Jewel Orb (Anatomy I1, Status: BUILT — "Law")
text: - "Colored glass sphere carrying the spectrum color. The family signature." (Anatomy §2.3 I1.) - Also law: I4 Initial Orb ("every person is a color") and I9 Pulse Dot ("a small orb whose color and pulse say the state"). - Icons are drawn, not shrunk (DESIGN-LAWS.md, Law 4): "Native vector geometry — bold, simple, luminous, readable at 16px... every glyph must promise its real behavior... A beautiful but inert affordance is unfinished." Bullets are jewels (rotated-square diamonds), not dots.

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] Inputs — the Well (Anatomy N1, Status: BUILT — "Law: inputs are wells")
text: - "Dark recessed channel, carved inset shadow, white text. The inverse of a button — you press INTO it." (Anatomy §2.4 N1.) Same laws, inverted depth: a button presses back, a well receives.

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] Gauges and charts — the Orbit Dial and the Living Line (Anatomy G4/G1, Status: BUILT)
text: - G4 Orbit Dial: "A radial gauge — the needle reads the live value, the dial is the Smart Score." G1 Living Line: "A trend line drawn from real ledger data — tap any bar/point, its records open." (Anatomy §2.5.) - The Playbook's gauge is the living example of the whole system: vortex mathematics, obsidian + aluminum materials, top-left light, slow motion (Playbook, "How to access this": "look at the gauge — it's the living example of everything in here").

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] Smart apps, pages, sections — one app, many doors
text: - NAYA Protocol §5 (The One App): "NayaNET is ONE ultimate app with different doors... Same dashboard behind every door. Same mail. Same smart notes. Same smart lists. One ledger." - Real Object Law, Viewpoint Law: "Every screen is a VIEWPOINT — its own object, its own world, its own purpose... Every element is real, active, alive — a machine that's running, not a picture of one." - Sections follow the same laws at larger scale: the Hub's rooms wear one accent color each ("one distinct color per room — never two rooms alike", Hub file `:root` comment; `--accent-feed: #a06bff`, "grape royal purple — the main page wears the soul color (Shawn 2026-10-20)"). ---

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] PART 4 — THE INTELLIGENT BLOCK, SECTION BY SECTION
text: The board is built by `renderIntelBoard(note, idx, stream)` in `HUB/app/index.html` (working copy `~/workspace/team-nitro/hub-board-edit/index.html`, v4). It renders an `<article class="intel-board tone-<note.tone || 'purple'>">`. Every formatting value below is from that file's CSS/JS unless another source is named. Where the file contradicts itself or the laws, the conflict is listed in CONFLICTS and the rule is stated as "contested", not as settled.

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] 4.0 THE BOARD ITSELF
text: - **Purpose:** the grand block — the elite of all blocks, carrying every design law all the way through (Shawn 00:08Z; MEMORY.md, HUB BOARD LAW amendment). One Smart Note, one board, in the feed. - **Theme:** obsidian black at rest; spectrum lives in the jewel, the edge, and the light — never as ambient wash (Anatomy §1.4 law 12; DESIGN-LAWS.md Law 2). - **Color:** its own tone, from the note (`tone-<note.tone || 'purple'>`; default purple). Tone classes in the file: purple, sapphire, emerald, indigo, forest, lime, gold, orange, ruby, magenta. Board theme rotation comment: "purple → sapphire → emerald (canonical spectrum order)". How a live note's tone is chosen is a GAP (G2). - **Elements:** block top (jewel + title + meta, plus truth badge); quote (subtitle); date line; nutshell; layers; provenance foot; social actions (top-right + bottom bar). The board also gets class `board` and a `boardId` (`note-<id>`). - **Formatting (base rules, before the v4 overrides):** `--tone: var(--purple)`; border 2px solid `color-mix(in srgb, var(--tone) 55%, #fff 14%)`; radius 26px (phone: 20px, padding 22px 18px 18px); padding 32px 32px 24px; background: radial gradient (720px 240px at 50% -8%, tone 14% → transparent 72%) over `linear-gradient(145deg, var(--bg-raise), var(--bg))`; box-shadow: `inset 0 1px #ffffff2e`, `0 28px 64px #000000c0`, `0 0 44px color-mix(in srgb, var(--tone) 18%, transparent)`; `overflow: hidden`. - **The elevated edge light:** `.intel-board::before` — a 4px vertical …

title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] 4.1 TITLE / QUOTE AREA (the top of the board — NOT an inner board)
text: - **Purpose:** identity — what this note is, in one headline; then the note's own words as a quote. - **Theme:** the note's headline + its voice, centered. - **Color:** title and quote are white text on the black board (`--ink` / `#fff`); color lives in the jewel and the edge, not the words (L5). - **Elements:** `.ib-blocktop` (flex, space-between, gap 16px, align flex-start, margin-bottom 6px) holding `.ib-identity` (flex, gap 14px) — the jewel (`.ib-jewel`, 64×64) + title + meta — and the truth badge; then `.ib-subtitle` (the quote). - **Formatting — title:** CONTESTED — three `.ib-title` rules in the file (see CONFLICT C3): (a) `clamp(24px, 2.8vw, 32px)`, line-height 1.12, letter-spacing -0.01em, margin 0 0 20px, weight 800; (b) `clamp(24px, 3vw, 38px)`, line-height 1.05, letter-spacing -.02em, margin 0 0 8px, weight 850; (c) phone: `clamp(24px, 6.4vw, 32px)`. title: [BLOCK-RULES-LAW] 4.2 DATE / META LINE
text: - **Purpose:** when this note was entered, and which note it is — provenance at a glance. - **Theme:** quiet metadata, small and dim but readable — it sits under the quote, not competing with it. - **Color:** `#817a89` (muted gray-violet) for the meta text; the date itself renders in the board's tone color in the live screenshots (green date in the 00:06Z screenshot) — the tone-colored date is observed, not pinned to a rule in the file (GAP G3). - **Elements:** `.ib-meta` (flex, gap 8px, wrap; font-size 11px, weight 800, letter-spacing .08em, color `#817a89`); a `Note ` is added when the headline was derived; a timestamp line ("when this note was entered — one consistent seat in the card", comment dated Shawn 2026-10-21). - **Formatting:** 11px / 800 / .08em letter-spacing; spans `white-space: nowrap`. - **What it says:** the full date and time ("Thursday, November 5, 2026 3:07 PM") plus a relative age ("· 59 min ago"). Relative age comes from `timeAgo(ts)`: under 60s "just now"; under 60m "Xm ago"; under 24h "Xh ago"; else "Xd ago" (a second function, `relTime(iso)`, gives the same ladder and falls back to `toLocaleDateString()` after 7 days). The exact composition of the full-date + relative line is not pinned to one function in the file — GAP G3.
